sn12.52:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases.
sn12.52:1.3: With craving as condition, clinging comes to be;
sn12.52:1.6: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.52:1.7: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.52:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, a great bonfire was burning, consuming ten, twenty, thirty, or forty loads of wood,
sn12.52:2.2: and a man would cast dry grass, dry cowdung, and dry wood into it from time to time.
sn12.52:2.3: Thus, sustained by that material, fuelled by it, that great bonfire would burn for a very long time.
sn12.52:2.4: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases….
sn12.52:2.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.52:3.1: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases.
sn12.52:3.2: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging;
sn12.52:3.3: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence …
sn12.52:3.5: aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.52:3.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.52:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, a great bonfire was burning, consuming ten, twenty, thirty, or forty loads of wood,
sn12.52:4.2: and a man would not cast dry grass, dry cowdung, or dry wood into it from time to time.
sn12.52:4.3: Thus, when the former supply of fuel is exhausted, that great bonfire, not being fed with any more fuel, lacking sustenance, would be extinguished.
sn12.52:4.4: So too, when one lives contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases….
sn12.52:4.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
